_comment: STARTER FILE. Copy me into contracts/examples/<your_tool_name>.json, fill every TODO, delete the _comment keys, and open a PR. Your editor will red-underline mistakes before CI ever sees them.

interface._comment: WHAT THE TOOL IS. This layer maps 1:1 to the standard MCP tool shape, so any MCP client can consume it.
interface.name: TODO_snake_case_name
interface.title: TODO Human Readable Title
interface.description: TODO one sentence, at least 20 characters, saying what this returns. The agent reads this to decide whether to pick you.
interface._comment_hints: whenToUse / whenNotToUse are the selection hints. Be concrete -- these are the difference between the agent picking you correctly and picking you by accident.
whenToUse: TODO a concrete situation where this tool is the right pick.
whenNotToUse: TODO a situation where the agent should reach for something else.

input._comment_forbidden: Optional. Field names a caller must never be able to supply.

response._comment_ui: Optional render hint. {braces} interpolate fields from the response.

binding._comment: WHERE IT CALLS. Use type 'http' for a real API, or type 'none' with a builtin:// handler for a pure function that runs inside the engine with no network.

http._comment_auth: Reference a secret by NAME. Never paste the value into a contract.

validation._comment: Optional. These regexes are compiled into the generated code as real guards.

_comment_dependencies: Declared for documentation only -- the POC engine does not resolve these.

governance._comment: HOW IT IS ALLOWED TO RUN. This layer is ours; MCP leaves it open.
governance._comment_annotations: readOnly drives caching. A destructive tool is never cached, and the schema enforces that.
governance._comment_execution: 'direct' runs immediately. 'propose-apply' returns a proposal and waits for a human -- it requires humanApproval 'required'.
governance._comment_caching: keyBy picks which args form the cache key. Omit it to key on all of them.
